line00
Your first freelance year has a calendar, and missing it costs money.
line01
Month one: open a separate tax account. Our example puts two seventy from every thousand in it.
line02
Keep every receipt, and a kilometre log if you drive for work. The C-R-A can ask for six years of records.
line03
Pass thirty thousand in sales over four quarters in a row, and you'll need a G-S-T number.
line04
December thirty-first: for most sole proprietors, the business year ends.
line05
Then you have sixty days to put money into an R-R-S-P and deduct it for that year.
line06
April thirtieth: pay it all. With no instalments yet, the whole bill lands at once.
line07
June fifteenth: file your return. Interest on unpaid tax already started May first.
line08
Year two: if the bill was over three thousand, instalment reminders can start.
line09
Next: taxes on creator and platform income. Follow so you don't miss it.
